name: Learn Morse code well enough to recognise common letters
blurb: Learn it by sound from the start — as rhythms, never as dots and dashes on a page — and the common letters become recognisable within a fortnight.
gear: A Morse trainer app using the Koch or Farnsworth method
steps: Learn by sound only. Reading dots and dashes visually creates a translation step you will spend months unlearning.
Use the Koch method: start with just two characters at full speed, adding one more each time you hit 90% accuracy.
Learn characters as rhythmic sounds — “dah-di-dah-dit” as a single unit, not four events.
Learn the high-frequency letters first: E, T, A, I, N, M, S, O.
Practise 15 minutes daily. Little and often matters far more here than long sessions.
Learn SOS and your own name and callsign to fluency.
tips: Never use a chart that shows dots and dashes visually. It is the single biggest cause of a permanent speed ceiling.
Full character speed with long gaps (the Farnsworth approach) is far better than slowing the characters down.
proof: You copy a short plain-text message by ear at 10 words per minute.
